name: GGUF Q5_K_M (5-bit K-quant, medium)
quality_delta: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.40 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.08); GSM8K 64.35 vs 77.63 (-13.28, the study's clearest multi-step-reasoning regression among the 5-bit tier); IFEval 72.33 vs 78.93; unweighted mean 69.36 vs 69.47; size 5460 MiB (-64.35%).
notes: The 5-bit K-quant tier is the study's accuracy-recommended regime, but note it recommends *Q5_0* (legacy 5-bit) over Q5_K_M on the compression/quality frontier - a claim that contradicts the usual 'newer K-quants are better' assumption and is why this record is contested. Q5_K_S is the weirder outlier: same 5.5704-class size as Q5_0 but a notably worse GSM8K (65.19 in its table vs 79.08). Weight-only: activations stay in FP16/BF16 at runtime, so there is no '4-bit activations with hardware support' claim to make here. ggml has bespoke dequantize+gemm kernels per type, but no accelerator has a GGUF/k-quant path in silicon; everything is dequantized on the fly. vLLM explicitly labels its GGUF support experimental and under-optimized and positions it as a memory-footprint tool (quant-vllm-gguf-doc). Perplexity ordering within 5-bit (7.43 for Q5_0/Q5_1/Q5_K_S, 7.40 Q5_K_M) is nearly flat while GSM8K spans 64-79: ppl is a poor proxy for reasoning quality, and llama.cpp's own CPU decode table shows Q5_K_M at 67.23 tok/s vs Q6_K 58.67 and Q8_0 50.93 (quant-llamacpp-quantize-readme).
